task_description.overview: Compute frequency–wavenumber (FK) power spectra from seismic array data to estimate backazimuth and slowness of a seismic source.
steps: Load multi‐channel seismic waveform data from a file or URL into an ObsPy Stream object.
Assign instrument response (PAZ) and station coordinates to each Trace.
Apply instrument correction to standardize to a desired corner frequency.
Define FK processing parameters: slowness grid bounds and step, time window length and fraction, frequency band, prewhitening, and detection thresholds.
Run ObsPy’s array_processing() on the preprocessed Stream to compute time‐dependent relative power, absolute power, backazimuth, and slowness.

task_definition.agent_prompt:
Perform FK analysis on the seismic array data loaded from {waveform_source}. Set station PAZ and coordinates information to the tr.stats.paz and tr.stats.coordinates, apply instrument correction to {corn_freq_2_paz.corner_frequency_hz} Hz by using the `corn_freq_2_paz` and `st.simulate` function, then run `array_processing(st,**fk_parameters)`. Return an ndarray with columns [timestamp, rel_power, abs_power, backazimuth, slowness]. With the calculated FK output array from array_processing(), generate a 4‐panel time‐series scatter plot for relative power, absolute power, backazimuth, and slowness over time. Color the points by relative power and format the x‐axis as dates. 
 Note: 1) Save the fk analysis plot to {result_plot}.
